extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and agents submitting mystery/crime/suspense works for consideration in the Edgar® Awards (Mystery Writers of America)
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility and submission guidelines for works (books, short stories, television) to the Mystery Writers of America's Edgar® Awards for works first published/produced in the U.S. during the specified calendar year. Covers general rules (publisher, payment, year of publication) and category-specific format, citizenship, length, and content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: First U.S. publication/production year
rubrics_metrics.description: All books, short stories and television shows are eligible if they were published or produced for the first time in the U.S. during the calendar year of consideration (2026 for the 2027 awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only works first published/produced in the United States during the calendar year qualify. Television episodes must have been shown for the first time in the United States in the eligibility year. Copyright date shall prevail over publication date in determining the year of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-published works and U.S. availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Books from non-U.S. publishers are eligible only if they are widely distributed in the U.S. and readily available on shelves in brick-and-mortar stores for the first time during the eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special order titles do not qualify. If a foreign book has an earlier copyright, the year of consideration is the year of its first U.S. publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-published works ineligible / reprints ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: At this time, self-published work is not eligible for Edgar Award consideration; a self-published book later republished by an Approved Publisher is considered a reprint and does not qualify as a new work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A republished self-published work may qualify a writer for Active Status membership but will not qualify for Edgar Award consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved publisher requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The work must be published by a publisher on MWA’s approved publisher list to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a publisher wishes to be added to the approved list they must contact the MWA national office to begin vetting; requests must be approved by the national board before the final submission deadline for a work to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author payment / Active Status eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The work itself must pay enough to make the author eligible for MWA Active Status or count toward earning that status, and the author must have received payment by the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: to be eligible, a short story must be published by an MWA-approved publisher and the author must have received at least $25 from that publisher in advance money or royalties before the story is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-committee submission rule (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A work may be submitted to only one committee except for specifically named award exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are the Robert L. Fish Award, the Mary Higgins Clark Award, the Lilian Jackson Braun Award, and the Sue Grafton Memorial Award. Submission of a work to the wrong category will result in disqualification; it is the ultimate responsibility of the publisher/author to ensure correct category submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright-year vs publication-year exception process
rubrics_metrics.description: If publication is delayed beyond the author's control such that a work with a copyright of one year is not published until the following year, the work may be submitted in the year of publication under strict conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: the work must not have been submitted in any form during the copyright year; the author must petition the General Awards Chair and the chair of the appropriate awards committee and send a statement from the publisher stating the work was not available during the copyright year. No work can be submitted in both the copyright year and the publication year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Novel — format and first-novel citizenship rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Novel entries must be hardbound only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First novels by U.S. citizens are not eligible for this category and must be submitted under Best First Novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best First Novel — format, citizenship, and prior-publication exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Best First Novel accepts hardbound, paperback or e-book originals and is limited to first-time novelists holding U.S. citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an American author publishing his or her first mystery has previously published a novel of any type (except if it is self-published), even under a different name, they are ineligible for Best First Novel. Non-American writers are ineligible for Best First Novel but may submit to Best Novel or Best Paperback/E-Book categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Paperback/E-Book Original — format and citizenship nuances
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for paperback or e-book original novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paperback or e-book first novels by U.S.-born authors are not eligible for this category and must be submitted under Best First Novel; foreign authors may submit a paperback or e-book first novel in this category. E-Book publishers must be on MWA’s Approved E-Book publishers list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Fact Crime — nonfiction scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Fact Crime is for nonfiction only (hardbound, paperback or e-book).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category includes books about actual crimes as well as those detailing how to solve actual crimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Critical/Biographical — subject scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Critical/Biographical accepts hardbound, paperback or e-book works that are critical studies or biographies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Biographical' refers to biographies of mystery writers or notable practitioners of the genre; biographies of criminals should be submitted to Best Fact Crime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Short Story — source and length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible short stories must be from magazines, periodicals, e-zines, or book-length anthologies and be between 1,000 and 22,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories under 1,000 words (mini- or flash fiction) do not qualify. Stories over 22,000 words should be submitted to Best Novel, Best First Novel, or Best Paperback Original/E-Book categories. This committee also selects the Robert L. Fish Memorial Award for best published mystery short story by a previously unpublished American author; when submitting for the Fish Award, note this on the entry form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Juvenile Mystery — age range and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Juvenile Mystery entries must be fiction and published in hardbound or paperback formats for readers Preschool up to Grade 7 (ages 5–12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category excludes Young Adult works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Young Adult Mystery — age range and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Young Adult Mystery entries must be fiction and published in hardbound or paperback formats for Grades 8–12 (ages 13–18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Television Series Episode Teleplay — submission form and airing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a PDF (no watermarks) of the final script of episodes that have actually aired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only final teleplays of episodes that have been broadcast/aired in the U.S. during the eligibility year are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sue Grafton Memorial Award — series position, protagonist type, and setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to a book that most closely fits Sue Grafton/Kinsey Milhone hallmarks: at least the second in a series and featuring a female protagonist with certain traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally required a female protagonist with quirks, self-knowledge, empathy, savvy, intelligence, and wit. Criteria broadened to include any book featuring a strong, independent woman who is a professional investigator (private eyes, crime-beat journalists, attorneys, law enforcement). Eligible works must be set in contemporary times between 1980 and the present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mary Higgins Clark Award — tradition/style/content restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Award given to the book most closely written in the Mary Higgins Clark tradition with specific protagonist characteristics and content limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protagonist is a nice young woman whose life is suddenly invaded; she is self-made and independent with primarily good family relationships; she has an interesting job; she is not looking for trouble and solves her problem by her own courage and intelligence. The story has no on-scene violence and contains no strong four-letter words or explicit sex scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lilian Jackson Braun Award — contemporary cozy mystery criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for the best full-length, contemporary cozy mystery honoring Braun’s legacy, with specific length, publication, tone, setting, and resolution requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book must be full-length (65,000 words or more) and first published by an MWA-approved publisher during the calendar year prior to the award; reprints are not eligible. The book must be a contemporary cozy mystery with a current-day setting emphasizing solving a crime (usually a murder). Historical mysteries, even if cozy, do not qualify (some historical elements are allowed if emphasis remains on contemporary investigation). Tone is light and often humorous; serious themes must be handled non-heavy-handedly. The crime must be solved satisfactorily by the end of the story. Additional qualifying criteria are linked on the MWA site.
